verified.entry_point: HTTP requests through a Fastify server built from /workspace/fastify.js and driven with fastify.inject(). Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: 14 security tests fail because a request schema of false (or an unapplied schema) is treated as absent and the handler runs; 12 functional tests pass. On the reference fix all 26 pass. The same tree also runs the project's own schema-feature, route, validation and 404 suites (244 cases), green before and after.
sites: lib/validation.js:230 - headers branch: `headers !== undefined` (injected tree: `if (headers && ...)`; false skipped, and the boolean never reaches the header-name normalisation)
lib/validation.js:246 - body branch: `schema.body !== undefined` (injected tree: `if (schema.body)`; false and null skipped)
lib/validation.js:262 - querystring branch: `schema.querystring !== undefined` (injected tree: truthiness)
lib/validation.js:268 - params branch: `schema.params !== undefined` (injected tree: truthiness)
lib/route.js:422 - validator-compiler setup: `hasValidationSchema` uses !== undefined (injected tree: `opts.schema.body || ...`, so no compiler is installed for a false-only schema)
lib/schemas.js:64 - the documented query alias is materialised into querystring before the compiler runs (injected tree: `if (routeSchemas.query)`)

lib/four-oh-four.js:149 - the not-found handler context stores opts.schema but nothing normalises or compiles it, so every schema declared there is ignored; the oracle also sets attachValidation:false on that context, which the request path needs to treat a validation error as a refusal
lib/schema-defaults.js:28 - injected server-wide default merge: `defaultSchema[part] !== undefined` (injected tree: `defaultSchema[part]`, so a false default is dropped); applied at lib/route.js:212
lib/request.js:346 - injected request-time inline validation helper: `schema === undefined` (injected tree: `if (!schema)`, so false is treated as no schema)
routes_investigated_not_built: schema.body.content[<type>].schema === false: the pinned tree refuses the route at ready with FST_ERR_SCH_CONTENT_MISSING_SCHEMA (fail-closed, no request can reach it); left as is, not a bypass.
schema.response (serialization): a different protection over response data; outside this advisory's request-validation property.

validateSchemaBodyOption (lib/route.js:617): a body schema on a bodyless method is refused at registration for objects but accepted for false; this is a registration-time guard and fail-closed, so no request bypass exists.
request.validateInput(data, false): the existing inline-schema API rejects non-object schemas with FST_ERR_REQ_INVALID_VALIDATION_INVOCATION (fail-closed). Kept as-is; it is not a bypass.
auto-generated HEAD route: shares the GET route's schema and the same compile path; covered by a security test but not a separate lever.
injected_siblings: S1 - lib/schema-defaults.js plus fastify.setDefaultSchema: server-wide default request-part schemas merged into routes that do not declare that part. Reachable through the normal route registration API; the published fix never touches the module or the method.

S2 - lib/request.js validateSchema: an inline request-time validation helper next to the existing compileValidationSchema/getValidationFunction/validateInput APIs. Reachable from any hook or handler; the published fix never touches request.js.
verified.project_tests_run: test/schema-feature.test.js, test/route.7.test.js, test/validation-error-handling.test.js, test/internals/validation.test.js, test/internals/request-validate.test.js, test/404s.test.js (244 cases), restored from pristine copies at grading time and run with node --test; 244 pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected outcome is whether a request is validated before its handler; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource whose authorisation could be decided instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles or directions exist on this path; one presence decision covers every request part and every HTTP method.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the presence decision is on the schema value itself, not on a parsed spelling or identity, so a malformed spelling cannot make it see nothing.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, secret or role lookup exists on this path, so no fix has a lookup that could fail open.

traps.lever_type: where (four request parts + compiler setup) with a coupled how (explicit-undefined semantics)
traps.shape: a route request schema of the boolean false for the body, headers, querystring or params, through the shorthand and the extended route API, and on multi-method routes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report's own value; once the four request-part branches are changed, every ordinary repro passes, and the compiler-setup gate in route.js is easy to miss because a false-only route then fails at ready instead of serving requests

traps.lever_type: where (second producer) + how (a presence decision after the alias adjustment)
traps.shape: a request schema written under the documented alternative name for the query-string part, with the value false
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the alias lives in a schema-normalization module that has nothing to do with validation; the canonical part is covered and the alias reads as plumbing

traps.pattern: B (uncovered route: the protection never existed there)
traps.lever_type: how (a route where the protection never existed)
traps.shape: a request schema declared on the handler for unmatched URLs - the deny-all boolean and an ordinary object schema - with the handler running for every request
traps.where: lib/four-oh-four.js:149 (context created, schema stored, never compiled)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the option is undocumented and absent from the typings; the fallback for unmatched URLs never validated any schema of any shape, so it reads as an unrelated pre-existing gap; and the published fix never touches it

traps.pattern: A (coupled must-keep-working value next to the sink)
traps.lever_type: how (a shape a plausible presence check mishandles)
traps.shape: a request part explicitly set to undefined (must warn and start), a non-schema value such as null (must fail closed), the boolean true (must admit), a per-route custom validator compiler receiving the literal boolean, and attachValidation staying effective
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a (behavioural lever; the over-broad presence test is caught by overbroad.patch, expect functional_fail)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: presence by key (hasOwn / in) looks like the same fix and passes every deny-all repro, but it compiles the explicitly-undefined part and breaks the documented warning-and-start behaviour

traps.lever_type: how (a producer/merge off the compiler's path)
traps.shape: a server-wide default request schema whose value is false, applied to a route that does not declare that part
traps.reason_to_dismiss: defaults are a convenience around the route's own schema, and a merge written as 'only fill in what the route did not set' looks complete; the value false is dropped by the same truthiness the report is about, in code the published fix never touches
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a maintainer adding server-wide default request schemas next to addSchema/setValidatorCompiler

traps.lever_type: how (a second presence decision in a request-time helper)
traps.shape: an inline schema of false passed to the request's validation helper from a handler; the helper reports the data as valid and the handler continues
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an imperative call made by the application at request time reads as the application's own check rather than route configuration, and the helper's early return for a 'missing' schema looks like ordinary defensive code; the published fix never touches request.js
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a convenience wrapper next to the existing compileValidationSchema / getValidationFunction / validateInput request APIs
